devon_support: Heads-up: multiple customers hitting 503s for hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. Errors show upstream runner exiting 139/137. Example log:
```
2026-03-17T09:11:52Z ERROR upstream_runner: exit_code=139 signal=SIGSEGV model=redwood-v2 batch=8
2026-03-17T09:11:52Z WARN request_gateway: 503 returning to client
```
Anyone seen this? @maria_sre @sam_infra

maria_sre: I'm on it. Which hosts/regions? Any correlation to deployments?

devon_support: Mostly us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Affected customers are on a mix of model sizes but the failures spike with long seqs (>1536) and larger batches (>=8).

sam_infra: We rolled runtime image infer-runtime:2026.03.17-optim at 07:00 UTC — that touched an attn-kernel optimization and a prefetch change. Rolling back if needed. Pulling pod logs now.

opsbot: Alert: infer-runner pod infer-runner-7f9c (us-west-2a) terminated with signal 11. Core dump uploaded to s3://redwood-dumps/2419991111/infer-runner-7f9c.core.gz

igor_ml: Recent attention-kernel tweak + prefetch change landed in that runtime. Could be a regression on long sequences. If someone can preserve a core and run a bt I'll try to map to kernel symbols.

qa_jordan: I tried to repro with a small harness. Repro steps: `python stress.py --model redwood-v2 --seq 2048 --batch 12 --qps 10` — got CUDA OOM followed by segfault. From logs: `CUDA OOM at attn_kernel.cu:453` then `signal 11` and process exit.

maria_sre: Collect these: `kubectl cp namespace/inferrunner:/core core.gz` or if live: `kubectl exec -n hosted -it infer-runner-7f9c -- gdb --batch --ex 'thread apply all bt' --pid $(pidof runner)` — don't delete cores, upload to S3. Also capture `nvidia-smi -q` and driver logs.

sam_infra: I'm toggling routing to fallback runtime: `redwoodctl routing set --model '*' --to infer-runtime:2026.03.01-stable --percent 100` to stop new pods from pulling the broken image.

liz_prod: :rotating_light: Customer impact: 5 paying customers reporting timeouts and degraded UX. CSMs notified and asking for ETA — need quick mitigation and a statement.

devon_support: Noted. Temporary customer guidance: reduce `batch_size` to <=4 and limit `max_tokens`/`max_sequence` to 1024; this avoids the attn kernel path that seems to blow memory. I'll push a KB.

igor_ml: Agreed — short-term workaround: batching.max_per_request=4 and max_sequence=1024. Long-term: rollback kernel patch and run a canary harness across the seq-length distribution with memchecks. I'll start a repro matrix.

maria_sre: Rolled routing back at 09:28 UTC to stable runtime. 503 count dropped ~2m after change but some pods that were already on the bad image keep restarting. Collecting core stacks now.

opsbot: Deploy-bot: rollout infer-runtime:2026.03.01-stable completed at 09:30 UTC. 0 failing replicas reported in us-west-2 after re-provisioning. Core uploads finished: s3://redwood-dumps/2419991111/ (3 cores).

sam_infra: Action items assigned: 1) maria_sre — preserve cores + full bt + env; 2) igor_ml + qa_jordan — reproduce minimal case + test patch; 3) sam_infra — coordinate routing and prepare canary; 4) liz_prod — customer comms/postmortem owner. I'm available to coordinate on-call.

devon_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update customers with the temporary workaround and note we've rolled back the runtime. Please post ETA for root cause and a follow-up in this thread. :thumbsup:

liz_prod: Please also include a note whether any billed requests were retried/duplicated due to 503s — finance wants that flagged for potential credits.

maria_sre: Will add billing check to postmortem checklist (search logs for status=503 and retry headers). I'll upload preliminary stack traces within the hour.

(incident thread summary: runtime optimization introduced attn-kernel regression for long sequences leading to CUDA OOM -> SIGSEGV -> pod exit -> 503s; mitigation = rollback runtime routing, preserve cores, reproduce and patch.)
